items.title: Lindsay Clancy Will Be Retried in Murder Case, New Trial Date Scheduled
items.summary:
Lindsay Clancy will be retried in her murder case, with Judge William Sullivan declaring that her new trial will begin on March 29, 2027.

Clancy, 36, appeared in Plymouth Superior Court on Monday, November 16, to discuss the future of her case after her mistrial in September. During the latest hearing, prosecutors shared their plans to retry Clancy, according to CBS News .

After the commonwealth argued that the retrial should begin in May, Sullivan, 69, pushed for a March date. (Sullivan previously announced his plans to retire in 2027.)

Sullivan has made several rulings regarding the case since the last hearing on November 9, in which he denied Clancy’s motion to dismiss the murder charges.

Judge Denies Lindsay Clancy Lawyer’s Latest Bid to Drop Her Murder Charges 

Plymouth County District Attorney Tim Cruz has the final say in retrying Clancy on first-degree murder charges and has the power to try Clancy on a lesser charge, such as second-degree murder or manslaughter.

Clancy was previously charged with murder in connection to the deaths of her kids, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months , in January 2023.

She never denied killing her kids, but her defense argued that she should not be held criminally responsible because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time of the deaths. Meanwhile, the prosecution argued that she was aware of what she was doing and that her suicide attempt after the murders indicated the killings were intentional.

The jury deliberated for seven days until Sullivan declared a mistrial on September 4 when the jury said they…
items.t: Lindsay Clancy Will Be Retried in Murder Case, New Trial Date Scheduled

items.title: Dan Campbell Issues Update on Aidan Hutchinson Following Celebration Injury
items.summary:
Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell discussed a shocking injury to star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson , which came during a sack celebration on Sunday, November 16.  

“We’ll know more when we get back in the States,” Campbell, 50, told reporters after the Lions’ 35-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, on Sunday. “Anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today.” 

Hutchinson, 26, injured himself during the first quarter on Sunday after he jumped in the air to celebrate a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye .  

Maye, 24, was also hurt on the play and missed the rest of the game. ESPN reported on Monday, November 16, that Maye will miss “an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season.” 

Taylor Swift Seemingly Skips Chiefs-Falcons Game After CMA Awards Announcement 

While the Lions have not confirmed Hutchinson’s injury status, ESPN reported on Monday that he tore the ACL in his right knee and will miss the rest of the season.  

Hutchinson received an initial MRI in Germany before returning home with the team on Sunday. He is expected to undergo further testing in the coming days.  

The injury on Sunday is the latest in a string of unfortunate incidents for Hutchinson. In 2024, he broke the tibia and fibula in his left leg in Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys, forcing him to miss the rest of the season, including the Lions’ playoff loss to the Washington Commanders.  

Hutchinson…
items.t: Dan Campbell Issues Update on Aidan Hutchinson Following Celebration Injury

items.title: Taylor Swift Jokes About Being '0 for 8' for Grammys Song of the Year
items.summary:
Taylor Swift is finding humor in never winning the Grammys’ Song of the Year category.

The Recording Academy tapped Swift, 36, to help announce some of the nominations for the 2027 Grammys on Monday, November 16, which resulted in the pop star reflecting on her own history with the awards show.

“I’m very honored that the Grammys have asked me to be here to help reveal the last two categories for the Grammy nominations,” Swift, 36, said during Monday’s livestream.

She continued, “But I first wanted to start off by saying congratulations to anyone who is nominated for a Grammy this year in any category, because what this means is that your peers, your fellow musicians, producers, engineers, artists, writers, they love what you made.”

Grammy Awards 2027 Nominations: See the Complete List 

From Swift’s perspective, “that’s the coolest feeling in the world.” She noted in her message that she hopes the nominees “have a really wonderful day.”

“The last two categories to be announced, one of them I’ve had a lot of luck in. The other one I’m 0 for 8,” she said. “Here are the nominees for Album and Song of the Year.”

LISA O'CONNOR / AFP

items.title: Daphne Zuniga Addresses Future of 'Melrose Place' Podcast Amid Lengthy Pause
items.summary:
Daphne Zuniga is offering a rare update on her Melrose Place rewatch podcast with Courtney Thorne-Smith and Laura Leighton amid its ongoing pause.

“We did the first season and then our schedules all kind of split up,” Zuniga, 64, explained during an exclusive interview with Us on the set of Fox’s Celebrity Weakest Link . 

Zuniga hinted that they also “didn’t get the followers that we really needed.”

“We had passionate [listeners], but iHeartRadio had a quota and they just needed to make that,” she recalled about the podcast, which premiered in summer 2024. “And we’re like, ‘What about that theory of things will build?’ Then [Courtney and Laura] got busy. I was off shooting Spaceballs: The New One and everyone’s [working on something].”

'Melrose Place’ Stars on Plans to Modernize the Reboot for the Next Generation 

The actress, who played Jo Reynolds, didn’t rule out returning to the podcast project. “But we did get a call about would we want to revisit it? That was [a few] months ago,” she said. “So when things calm down, we might [return].”

She continued: “And it was just getting good because Melrose Place really got good when you get into all the big drama stuff, which was just happening at the end of the first season.”

Melrose Place , which ran from 1992 to 1999 , followed a group of young adults living in an apartment complex in West Hollywood. “It’s very difficult for me to process this incredible honor, because the truth is, I carry the epigenome of an outsider,” she said . “From the ages of 7 to 22, I was under the thumb of a very restrictive cult — don’t look at yourself in a mirror, no flirting, dress this way, talk this way, say it’s OK when your parents are routinely sent away from you for months on end. It meant that I was always on the outside looking in.”

Where Is Her Oscar?! Glenn Close Through the Years: Her Life in Photos 

Close went on to dedicate her award to her daughter and fellow actress, Annie Starke , and spoke about her previous brushes with Academy Awards glory.

“As an outsider, I was never worried about whether I was going to win or not, though some years I thought I might have a chance,” she said. “I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room. Over the past 43 years, I’ve been in the room eight times … not looking in the window, but in the room, part of this extraordinary community. So to be in this room tonight, embraced by the people who have consistently inspired me, whose work has sustained and challenged me and only made me want to be better, is the greatest honor of all.”

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.

The comedian, 51, is accused of having sex with a woman without her consent and then apologising afterwards, an investigation by the Times and the Sunday Times said.

items.title: Years of onscreen jokes suggest Walliams’ reputation was ‘in plain sight’ within industry, insider says
items.summary:
References raise questions over whether claims about bankable stars have been ignored by entertainment industry

The comedy sketch opens in a doctor’s office, with a trouserless David Walliams apparently being treated for a fictional sexually transmitted disease. The doctor tells him it is bad news and he needs to contact “everyone you’ve been intimate with over the last year”.

The camera closes in on the comedian’s shocked expression before he gasps: “Everyone?”
